title: (No AI) Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![Vector illustration of the Google Gemini logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25290329/STK255_Google_Gemini_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Google says its new [Gemini 4 Hydrogen](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/gemini-4-hydrogen-search-upgrade/) model can give more helpful answers to complex questions, including "questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests." The new model can break down your questions and address each part in its responses. It's [available starting today](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/) in search, the Gemini app, all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, and in Google Antigravity for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Robby Stein, VP of product at Google Search, [says](https://x.com/rmstein/status/2120941443359576166?a=lerZsroBaoIBT9jNz00&s=20) it's "now the new default model in AI Mode & being used for your hardest questions in AI Overviews."

title: (No AI) No, AI agents did not discover a previously unknown Maya site
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/maya-sites.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

“I woke up and checked the agents' reports. 'DAMN!' They had found lots of villages and other regular shapes that looked like structures or houses,“ Pietro Miotti wrote on his blog. | Image: [Pietro Miotti](//pietromiotti.com/latest/maya-site/”)

Armed with a team of AI agents, Google researcher Pietro Miotti claimed earlier this week to have discovered a potentially unmapped Maya site in Mexico. There was just one problem: The site had already been discovered and was published in an academic journal last year. The incident, which [sparked criticism](https://bsky.app/profile/indyfromspace.bsky.social/post/3n2235hwwsk2m) among archeologists online, underscores a growing tension in science as amateurs wielding increasingly powerful AI tools parachute into specialist fields, often without the expertise needed to understand what they are looking at.

> Local communities are often already well aware of sites in their area.
